sources.entry: Build an iOS App with SwiftUI

summary.title: Build an iOS app with SwiftUI
summary.one_liner: You learn SwiftUI basics by building a small iOS app that randomly recommends activities, covering shapes, images, text, stacks, buttons, state, and animation.
takeaways: Create a SwiftUI view and style it with modifiers such as fill, padding, overlay, font, and foregroundColor.
Arrange views with VStack and Spacer, and nest stacks to group content for animation.
Use @State (ideally marked private) to hold values that change while the app runs, and update them from a Button action.
Handle optionals from randomElement() using the nil-coalescing operator (??).
Animate changes with withAnimation and the id() and transition() modifiers.
summary.summary: This Swift.org guide walks through building a small iOS app called WhyNotTry in Xcode using SwiftUI, targeting iOS 16. It starts with a static UI built from a Circle, an SF Symbols Image, and Text, then adds a nested VStack layout and a title. It then introduces state, an array of activities, a "Try again" button, optionals, and @State. The final section adds polish: random colors, a Spacer, and a slide animation keyed by an id.
